definitions.explanation: A pungent yellow mustard paste made from ground mustard seeds, used as a condiment with natto, oden, tonkatsu, and other Japanese dishes. Sharper and hotter than Western mustards.

examples.japanese: {納豆|なっとう}にからしを{入|い}れる。
examples.english: I put mustard in my natto.

examples.japanese: おでんにからしをつけて{食|た}べた。
{練|ね}りからしは{少量|しょうりょう}でも{鼻|はな}にツンとくる{辛|から}さがある。
examples.english: Prepared karashi has a sharp, nose-tingling heat even in small amounts.

notes:
Written in kanji as {芥子|からし} or {辛子|からし}, but kana is most common on packaging and menus. Comes in tubes or small packets and is a standard accompaniment in Japanese cuisine.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {練|ね}りからし: prepared mustard paste (sold in tubes)
- {粉|こな}からし: powdered mustard
- からしを{添|そ}える: to serve with mustard on the side
- からし{醤油|じょうゆ}: mustard-soy sauce mixture

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マスタード: mustard — milder, Western-style; common with sausages and sandwiches
- わさび: wasabi — green Japanese horseradish, used with sushi and sashimi
- {柚子|ゆず}{胡椒|こしょう}: yuzu-pepper paste — different condiment, citrusy and spicy
